questions.text: List the characteristics of sole proprietorship organizations.
questions.text_as_printed: List the characteristics of sole proprietorship organizations. (A)

answer.value:
Characteristics of Sole Proprietorship
These are business organizations that have existed since ancient times.
They can be easily established.
Ownership belongs to a single individual; they are run for the owner's profit.
Owners invest their own capital and manage using their own skills.
No legal formalities are required to start or close them.
The owner is responsible for all losses of the business.
They may take help from family members.
In some cases, they employ workers for assistance.
Generally, they operate on a small scale.
Nowadays, some of these businesses are also organized on a larger scale.

questions.text: How is partnership business organizations formed?
questions.text_as_printed: How is partnership business organizations formed? (A)

answer.value:
To overcome the limitations of sole proprietorship, various types of business organizations came into existence; among them, partnership firms are one.
In these organizations, more than one person come together to carry on business.
To start and run partnership firms, the Partnership Act was enacted in 1932.
According to Section 4 of this Act, partnership is the relationship between persons who have agreed to share the profits of a business carried on by all or any one of them acting for all.
In banking business, the maximum number of partners is limited to ten, and in general partnership business, it is limited to twenty partners.

questions.text: Write about the business organizations under the Hindu Undivided Family (HUF) system.
questions.text_as_printed: Write about the business organizations under the Hindu Undivided Family (HUF) system. (A)

answer.value:
These types of business organizations exist only in India and are governed by Hindu law.
Male members of three successive generations continuously become members of this business organization.
These organizations consist of all male members of a Hindu family.
The senior-most male member of the undivided family supervises the business.
He is called the 'Karta'; though ownership belongs to all members, management is carried out by the Karta.
The liability of the Karta is unlimited.
The liability of other members is limited to the amount of capital invested by them.

solution_steps: These types of business organizations exist only in India and are governed by Hindu law.
Male members of three successive generations continuously become members of this business organization.
These organizations consist of all male members of a Hindu family.
The senior-most male member of the undivided family supervises the business.
He is called the 'Karta'; though ownership belongs to all members, management is carried out by the Karta.
The liability of the Karta is unlimited.
The liability of other members is limited to the amount of capital invested by them.
